# Open Source Europe

## Open Source Europe

- [Open Source Europe documentation](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/): Practical guidance for joining OSE, receiving funds and managing your Collective.
- [How to apply](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/getting-started/how-to-apply/): Use this guide to prepare and submit a hosting application, then understand OSE's review.
- [Eligibility](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/getting-started/how-to-apply/eligibility/): Open Source Europe (OSE) welcomes initiatives from around the world that align with our mission and values.
- [Application Questions](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/getting-started/how-to-apply/application-questions/): To streamline your application process with Open Source Europe (OSE), it’s beneficial to prepare answers to the following questions in advance.
- [Basics](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/basics/): This is your starting point after OSE accepts your Collective. Work through the essentials, then use the relevant guide for each transaction.
- [Financial Contributions – How to Donate](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate/): Helpful guides for Donors and Financial Contributors
- [Wire Transfer Instructions via Open Collective Platform](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate/wire-transfer-instructions-via-open-collective-platform/): Please note that all funds have this option available.
- [Applying for Grants](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate/applying-for-grants/): Use this guide when a funder may support your Collective through OSE.
- [Fundraising Tools & Resources](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate/fundraising-tools-and-resources/): More ways to raise funds
- [Setting up GitHub Sponsors](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate/setting-up-github-sponsors/): Guide to connecting GitHub Sponsors for Organizations to your Collective
- [Contributions in cryptocurrencies](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate/contributions-in-cryptocurrencies/): How OSE Collectives can receive cryptocurrency donations.
- [Refunds](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate/refunds/): Can I refund a donation or get a refund for one I have made?
- [Expenses](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/): Prepare a payment from your Collective's budget. Start by choosing the situation that matches your request.
- [Invoices or Reimbursements?](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/invoices-or-reimbursements/): Choose the request type before submitting an expense. Use Reimbursement if you have already paid; use Invoice when a supplier is requesting payment for…
- [Request a Grant (for Nonprofits Only)](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/request-a-grant-for-nonprofits-only/): In addition to submitting an expense or invoice, the Open Collective platform also includes the option to “Request a Grant.”
- [Expenses & Getting Paid – FAQs](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/expenses-and-getting-paid-faqs/): For the steps from planning a purchase to payment, start with the expense guide. This page answers specific payment questions.
- [The Partnership](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/the-partnership/): The relationship between your Collective and Open Source Europe (OSE) is one of indirect representation (représentation indirecte / middellijke…
- [VAT in Europe and How It Works in OCE](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/the-partnership/vat-in-europe-and-how-it-works-in-oce/): Collectives hosted by Open Collective Europe (OCE) are unincorporated initiatives primarily funded through donations.
- [Deciding on How to Use Your Money](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/guides/deciding-on-how-to-use-your-money/): How to use funds for your initiative on OSE
- [General FAQs](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/): What your initiative can do with Open Source Europe, what it costs, and how long it takes to get started.
- [Fiscal Hosting FAQs](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/fiscal-hosting-faqs/): A Fiscal Host is an organization that holds funds on behalf of Collectives, allowing them to operate financially without needing to establish a legal entity.
- [Expense FAQs](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/expense-faqs/): The detailed answers are maintained in Expenses & Getting Paid – FAQs. Use the links below to go directly to your question.
- [Contributions FAQ](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/contributions-faq/): Questions about contributing to our hosted collectives
- [Contact Us](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/about/contact-us/): For general inquiries, OSE aims to respond within seven business days, without a guaranteed response time.
- [Safeguarding Policy](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/about/safeguarding-policy/): Open Collective Europe (OCE) is committed to creating a safe and inclusive environment for all staff, volunteers, partners, and beneficiaries.
- [Mission, Vision & Impact areas](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/about/mission-vision-and-impact-areas/): It all comes back to resilience
- [Risk and Compliance aspects](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/about/risk-and-compliance-aspects/): Open Collective Europe: Grant Eligibility and Risk Assessment Policy
- [Community guidelines](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/about/community-guidelines/): These community guidelines reflect the values and commitments of Open Source Europe and aims to create a positive and productive community for all involved.
- [Terminology](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/about/terminology/): We have developed some terminology to describe processes within the Open Collective ecosystem. Please use these terms when creating issues or support requests, instead of user —everyone is a user!
- [What We Offer](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/): Open Source Europe provides the legal and financial infrastructure that open source projects need to thrive. Our services are designed to let you focus on your code, not on paperwork.
- [Umbrella organisation](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/umbrella-organisation/): Open Source Europe (OSE) provides a shared legal and financial framework for open source projects, developer networks, and software communities.
- [The Open Collective Platform](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/the-open-collective-platform/): A shared tool for managing contributions, expenses, and grants with full transparency.
- [Equivalency Determination Certificate](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/equivalency-determination-certificate/): Open Source Europe helps hosted projects receive grants from U.S. foundations through an Equivalency Determination (ED) arrangement.
- [Tax-Deductible Giving for U.S. Donors](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/tax-deductible-giving-for-us-donors/): U.S. individuals and businesses can support OSE Collectives through Myriad USA → Open Collective Europe Foundation (OCEF) → OSE.
- [About Open Source Europe](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/about-open-source-europe/): Open Source Europe is a Belgian Association that fiscally hosts over 400 initiatives and partners with philanthropic institutions to support global regranting.
- [Terms of Service](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/terms-of-service/): Hosting with Open Source Europe is governed by the association's Terms of Hosting.
